facts.statement: The type species Steneosaurus rostromajor was formally recognized in 2020.
facts.quote: The type species, S. rostromajor, was only formally recognised as such in 2020

facts.statement: The original specimen was discovered in three pieces by Abbot Charles Bacheley in the Vaches Noires near Villers-sur-Mer, France.
facts.quote: It was discovered in three pieces by abbot Charles Bacheley (1716-1795) in the Vaches Noires near Villers-sur-Mer (Calvados, France)

facts.statement: Georges Cuvier first illustrated the anterior pieces of the type specimen in 1808.
facts.quote: Georges Cuvier first illustrated in 1808 the two anterior pieces of the specimen kept in the Besson collection

facts.statement: Steneosaurus has historically served as a wastebasket taxon for many unrelated thalattosuchian fossils.
facts.quote: The genus has been used as a wastebasket taxon for thalattosuchian fossils for over two centuries

facts.statement: Due to an undiagnostic type specimen, the genus Steneosaurus is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: The genus Steneosaurus a nomen dubium

facts.statement: Species traditionally assigned to Steneosaurus are divided into longirostrine and mesorostrine skull groups.
facts.quote: Species in this genus are traditionally classed into two skull groups: longirostrine (long, narrow jaws) and mesorostrine (slightly shorter jaws)

facts.statement: A 2005 phylogenetic analysis found that Steneosaurus is not a monophyletic group.
facts.quote: A 2005 phylogenetic analysis into the evolutionary relationships of Thalattosuchia did not support the monophyly of Steneosaurus

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest the species 'Steneosaurus' obtusidens is the sister species of Machimosaurus and has been renamed Lemmysuchus.
facts.quote: Reinforcing the paraphyly of Steneosaurus, the Callovian species "Steneosaurus" obtusidens has been recovered as the sister species of Machimosaurus in recent cladistic analyses of Thalattosuchia and renamed Lemmysuchus

facts.statement: Steneosaurus belongs to the suborder Thalattosuchia and the family Teleosauridae.
Steneosaurus is an extinct teleosaurid crocodyliform that lived from the Middle Jurassic (Callovian).
facts.quote: Steneosaurus es un género extinto de crocodiliforme teleosáurido que vivió desde el Jurásico Medio (Calloviano)

facts.statement: The type species S. rostromajor lived in Western Europe (France) during the Callovian.
facts.quote: S. rostromajor: (especie tipo) Europa Occidental (Francia) del Calloviense

facts.statement: S. edwardsi lived in Western Europe (England and France) during the Callovian and Oxfordian.
facts.quote: S. edwardsi: Europa Occidental (Inglaterra y Francia) del Calloviano y el Oxfordiano

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Steneosaurus as Toarcian to Berriasian (184.2 to 141 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Berriasian (184.2 to 141 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether species currently labeled as Steneosaurus are related, as many are considered paraphyletic or polyphyletic.
facts.quote: The genus has remained a wastebasket, with numerous species still included under the label 'Steneosaurus', many of which are unrelated to each other (either paraphyletic or polyphyletic with respect to each other and other genera of teleosauroids)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the remaining species referred to Steneosaurus require new generic names.
facts.quote: The remaining species referred to Steneosaurus thus require new generic names
